title: Bina and tevuna in contemplating G-dliness: a summary of chapters 1 and 2

provenance.note: Ported from the demo's Markdown. Three things are coarser than a file written for this format: the phrases are whole paragraphs of Rabbi Markel's published translation (Sefaria, "The Gate of Unity", 2023, CC-BY), not phrases as translated in class; each block's word range starts where the demo's listen link pointed and its end is estimated (up to the next cited point, at most about 450 words); and the demo's style left out banter, stories and digressions, which `yarn study-check` lists as uncited stretches.

overview: Chapter three is a conclusion of the first two chapters, applying their terms to contemplating G-dliness, with the example of *memalei kol almin*, the coming into being of something from nothing. *Bina* is the essential grasp of the concept in all its particulars. Its length brings the concept close to the mind through physical analogies, until even a child can grasp it. Its width explains the same concept in many ways, through several lines of analogy. Only after length and width does one reach the depth, which can look like a brief summary but is not. *Daas* connects a person to what he has understood and leads to the sight of the intellect. *Tevuna* brings the hidden depth down into what one actually sees, until the world itself is seen as G-dliness. Without it, Chassidus stays an abstract idea, and a person asks what it is good for.

terms.gloss: the essential grasp of a G-dly concept in all its particulars
drawing the hidden depth of a concept down into revelation and into separate matters
(the light) that fills all worlds; the coming into being of something from nothing
the depth of the concept, how it is in its essence
close analysis; the vessel that leads to the depth
length; bringing the concept close to the mind through physical analogies
breadth; explaining the same concept in many different ways
spreading forth from the essence, as the soul's life in the body
revelation of what is hidden, as speech reveals thought
recognition and feeling; connection to the concept
sight of the intellect; seeing the truth of a matter, beyond following its explanation

sections.title: Bina in contemplating G-dliness: the example of memalei kol almin
sections.summary: Chapter three applies chapters one and two to contemplating G-dliness. Bina is the essential grasp of a G-dly concept, such as memalei kol almin, studied in all its particulars until one reaches its inner depth.

phrases.he: (ג) ובכל זה יובן בענין ההתבוננות בהשגת האלקות, שיש ב' מדריגות, בינה ותבונה. בינה היינו בחינת עצם ההשגה האלקית בכל פרט ענין שמתבונן, איך הוא ומה הוא, ועומד על הדבר בעיון רב בכל פרטי חלקיו כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: From all the above we understand that in the matter of contemplation (*Hitbonenut*) on the comprehension of G-dliness, there are two levels, *Binah* and *Tvunah*. *Binah* is the aspect of the essential comprehension of G-dliness, [to understand] every particular of the matter that he contemplates, [to understand] how and what it is. He keeps [his mind] upon the matter with a great analysis [to understand] all its particular components, as explained above.

blocks.text: This chapter is basically the conclusion of chapters one and two.
**From all the above we understand that in the matter of contemplation (*Hitbonenut*) on the comprehension of G-dliness, there are two levels, *Binah* and *Tvunah*.**
***Binah* is the aspect of the essential comprehension of G-dliness**, studying every particular of the matter, how it is and what it is, **with a great analysis**: that is, the actual learning.

phrases.he: כמו בהשגה פרטיות דממלא כל עלמין שהוא התהוות יש מאין הנקרא כח הפועל האלקי בנפעל כו'
phrases.en: An example of this [can be understood] from the comprehension of the details of *Memaleh Kol Almin* (the light of *HaShem*-יהו״ה, blessed is He, that fills all worlds). This is [the matter of] the coming into being of something from nothing, and is called, “the G-dly power and effect upon the affected.”

phrases.he: והוא בחינת שם אדנ״י או שם אלהי״ם, לשון כח כידוע. הנה יש בזה כמה חלוקי פרטים באופני חיצוניות הענין עד אשר יושג תוך תוך הענין הזה בפנימית העצמי, איך שהוא בעצם כו' שזהו הנקרא עומק המושג כו'
phrases.en: This is the aspect of the name *Adon”ai* (אדנ"י) or the name *Eloh”im* (אלהי״ם), which is a terminology of power, as known. In the externality of this matter there are many various particular facets [that one must understand], until he grasps the very inner [aspect of the] matter, [to understand] its inner essence, how it is essentially. This is what was called [above], “the depth of the concept” (*Omek HaMoosag*).
notes: See Ginat Egoz of Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla, translated as HaShem Is One, Vol. 1, The Gate of His Title (*Shaar HaKinuy*), and The Gate of the Sanctuary (*Shaar HaHeichal*).

blocks.text: The example is **the comprehension of the details of *Memaleh Kol Almin*** (the light that fills all worlds), which is **the coming into being of something from nothing**, called the G-dly power in what it affects (*koach hapoel banifal*).
This is the name *Adnus* or the name *Elokim*, names that mean power.

**In the externality of this matter there are many various particular facets**, until one grasps the very inside of the matter of *memalei kol almin*, how it is in its essence. **This is what was called [above], “the depth of the concept”** (*omek hamusag*).

sections.title: Length: bringing the concept close through analogies
sections.summary: Iyun is the vessel that leads to the depth. The length of bina brings the concept close to the mind by clothing it in physical analogies, until even a child can grasp it.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל שהעיון הוא בחינת כלי לבא לבחינת העומק כו' ובחינת האורך הוא בחינת התקרבות הענין הזה אל השכל במשלים שונים הידועים
phrases.en: We previously explained that the aspect of *Iyun* - analysis is the aspect of the vessel which brings one to the aspect of the depth. The length is the aspect of bringing the concept close to one’s intellect through the use of the various known analogies.

phrases.he: עד שיהיה הדבר הזה קרוב במוחו מאד (בל"א אראפ גילאזן זייער דעם שכל צו זיך) בלבוש הגשמה, עד שיוכל תינוק להשיג כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: [He does this] until the matter becomes very close to his mind, by investing it in physical [analogies], to the point that even a child can grasp it, as explained above.

blocks.text: **We previously explained that the aspect of *Iyun* - analysis is the aspect of the vessel which brings one to the aspect of the depth.**
**The length is the aspect of bringing the concept close to one’s intellect through the use of the various known analogies.**
This is the *orech* (length) of *bina*; the *iyun* (analysis) is what leads to its depth. Here the author is recapping what he has already said, so the lines are largely self-explanatory.
The length goes on **until the matter becomes very close to his mind**: in the Yiddish of the text, he has brought the intellect very close to himself.
It is done **by investing it in physical [analogies]**, since the analogies are a physical garment, **to the point that even a child can grasp it**.

sections.title: Width: one concept explained in many ways
sections.summary: Width explains the same concept in many ways. Memalei kol almin is explained through several lines of analogy, spreading from the essence and revealing the hidden, each with many analogies of its own; the opposite is a brief summary in one short way.

phrases.he: והרוחב היינו להרחיב זה הדבר כמו שהוא בכמה אופנים שונים, ולא באופן א' לבד
phrases.en: The width is to expand and explain how the matter is [manifest] in many different ways, as opposed to just a single way.

phrases.he: כמו המשל לזה הדבר מחיי הנפש בגוף, שאין זה רק התפשטות מן העצם כידוע
phrases.en: For example, an analogy for this matter [may be understood] from [how] the life force of the soul [is manifested] in the body. Now, this is only [the aspect of] a spreading forth from the essence, as known.

blocks.text: **The width is to expand and explain how the matter is [manifest] in many different ways, as opposed to just a single way.** That is the *rochav* (width).
**For example, an analogy for this matter [may be understood] from [how] the life force of the soul [is manifested] in the body.**
The life of the soul in the body is a *hispashtus min ha'etzem*, a spreading forth from the essence.

phrases.he: ויש רבוי אופנים למאוד בהתפשטות מן העצם וגם בגלוי ההעלם, כתנועת החי וכאותיות הדבור כו' או כהתחכמות מן עצם החכמה או כגלוי הראיה דעין או כגלוי שלהבת מן הגחלת כו' וכל זה נקרא גלוי ההעלם
phrases.en: There are a multitude of [other] ways [to understand the concept] of a spreading forth from the essence. Or, [regarding the concept] of the revelation of that which is hidden, [it may be understood] from [the analogy of] the movement of an animal, or from the letters of speech etc. [Another analogy is the flash of] insight from the essential *Chochmah*, or the revelation [of the power] of sight in the eye. [A further example is] the revelation of the flame from the coal. All the above are examples [of the concept] of the revelation of that which is hidden.
notes: For the explanations of each facet of the allegories presented here, see Rabbi Hillel Paritcher’s explanations to Shaar HaYichud, Chapter 3.

blocks.text: **There are a multitude of [other] ways [to understand the concept] of a spreading forth from the essence**: there are various analogies for spreading forth from the essence.

So *memalei kol almin* is explained in a few ways. One is the way of spreading forth from the essence, which has a number of analogies of its own. Another way is the *gilui ha'helem*, **the revelation of that which is hidden**.

That too has various forms: **the movement of an animal, or from the letters of speech**, **insight from the essential *Chochmah***, **the revelation [of the power] of sight in the eye**, **the revelation of the flame from the coal**.

Each one is a different way of saying or explaining it. **All the above are examples [of the concept] of the revelation of that which is hidden**, and all of them together are the width of one length, the revelation of the hidden.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן משל זיו השמש או אור הנר וכח הפועל כו' שנקרא התפשטות כו' וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: In contrast, the analogy of the ray of the sun, or the light of a candle, or an applied force of energy and the like, are analogies [for the concept] of a spreading forth [from the essence].

phrases.he: הרי כל זה בעצם הענין רק שנתרחב, וההיפך מזה הוא הקיצור רק באופן אחד, וגם הוא בדרך קצרה נסקר במוחו בלתי התפשטות להרחיב בו כלל כו'
phrases.en: All the above is the expansion on the essential matter. The opposite of this would be the short summation [and explanation of the concept] in only one way. Moreover, [in the summation, the explanation] itself is in a short way, [only] glanced [upon] by the mind, without any spreading forth to expand [his thoughts upon it] at all.

blocks.text: **In contrast, the analogy of the ray of the sun, or the light of a candle, or an applied force of energy and the like, are analogies [for the concept] of a spreading forth** from the essence.
That is a different length, and it too has various ways of being explained.
**All the above is the expansion on the essential matter**: all of it is still about the essence of *memalei kol almin*, only widened.

**The opposite of this would be the short summation [and explanation of the concept] in only one way**, which is narrow, and it is also short in length, **in a short way, [only] glanced [upon] by the mind**. So there is a shortness of width and a shortness of length.

sections.title: Depth: reached only after length and width
sections.summary: The depth of a concept, grasped after all the explanations and analogies, may look like the brief summary, but it is not. Everything chapter one said about keser, chachma and bina of bina applies to every particular G-dly concept, such as memalei kol almin.

phrases.he: אבל כמו שזה הדבר נתפס לעומקו בעצם, אחר כל רבוי הסבר דמיון המשלים, הוא הנקרא עומק ותמצית זה המושג כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: In contrast, the way this concept is grasped to its essential depth after the abundant explanations and comparative analogies, is called the depth and essence of this concept, as explained above.

phrases.he: ודווקא אחר האריכות והרוחב במשלים בעיון רב יבא לבחינת העומק שמובן מהם, (בל"א דער הערין דיא טיפקייט פון דעם וויא דיא זאך איז באמת) דהיינו אחר הלבשת חיצוניותו בכל העיון הרב כו' ודי למבין
phrases.en: It is specifically after the length and width of the [many] analogies and abundant analysis that he will come to the aspect of the depth that is understood through them. This is to say [that he will only reach the depth], through the external enclothements and abundant analysis. This will suffice those of understanding.

blocks.text: The brief summary just described is the shortness that comes before.
In contrast, **the way this concept is grasped to its essential depth after the abundant explanations and comparative analogies, is called the depth and essence of this concept**.

It looks the same as the brief version, but it really is not.

The depth after all the length and width can look like the short summary, yet the two are not the same.
**It is specifically after the length and width of the [many] analogies and abundant analysis that he will come to the aspect of the depth that is understood through them.**
The Yiddish in the text says it: to perceive the real depth of how the thing truly is.
With this the author has recapped chapter one in a single passage.

phrases.he: (וכל מה שכתבנו למעלה בכל פרטי כח''ב דבינה, הכל ימצא בהשגה פרטיות כזאת, וכהאי גוונא בכל השגת אלקות הפרטים9 וכמשי"ת)
phrases.en: (Everything that was previously explained regarding the particulars of *Keter, Chochmah* and *Binah* of *Binah* may be found in a particular concept such as this, and likewise, in every other particular concept in the comprehension of *HaShem*’s-יהו״ה G-dliness, as will be explained.)

blocks.text: So far he has explained *bina* and applied it to *memalei kol almin*.

*Bina* in it means going through the concept with all its particulars, all the different analogies and all the different explanations, whether of spreading forth or of revelation; that is the width. The length is bringing each one down into an analogy: for instance, the revelation of the hidden is like the letters of speech revealing the letters of thought, or it is the analogy of a river. The length makes it physical, bringing it down into physical terms.

**Everything that was previously explained regarding the particulars of *Keter, Chochmah* and *Binah* of *Binah*** refers to chapter one: *bina* of *bina* is *hisbonenus*; *chachma* of *bina* is discovering a new thing within the same thing; *Keser* is the *omek hamusag*, and the deeper *Keser* is the *shaar hanun* (the fiftieth gate).

All of it **may be found in a particular concept such as this**: in any particular comprehension throughout the book, the whole matter of *bina* will be found, as in *memalei kol almin*, **and likewise, in every other particular concept in the comprehension of *HaShem*’s-יהו״ה G-dliness, as will be explained** later in the book.

sections.title: Daas: connection to the concept, and the sight of the intellect
sections.summary: Daas is feeling and connection to what one has understood; the mitzva to know G-d is specifically in memalei kol almin. It leads to the depth of chachma, where the mind no longer follows an explanation but sees the truth.

phrases.he: ובחי' הדעת הוא בחינת ההכרה והרגשה במושכל בהתקשרות כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Now, the aspect of *Da’at* is the aspect of the recognition and feeling, that is, the connection to the concept, as explained above.

phrases.he: ועל זה נאמר וידעת כו' דע את אלה״י כו' שהוא בהשגה זו דממלא כל עלמין דוקא כידוע
phrases.en: About this it is stated, “*V’yadata* – You shall know [this day and set it upon your heart, that *HaShem*-יהו״ה, He is the G-d, in heaven above and on the earth below there is nothing else,” and “*Da et Elokei Avicha* *–* Know the G-d of your father etc.,” which refers specifically to the comprehension of how it is that *HaShem*’s-יהו״ה G-dliness fills all worlds, as known.

blocks.text: Now, **the aspect of *Da’at* is the aspect of the recognition and feeling, that is, the connection to the concept, as explained above.**
**About this it is stated**, “You shall know…” and “Know the G-d of your father…”, **which refers specifically to the comprehension of how it is that *HaShem*’s-יהו״ה G-dliness fills all worlds**.
The mitzva of *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d) is specifically in the matter of *memalei kol almin*, as the verse says, “the earth shall be full of knowledge of G-d as the waters cover the sea.”

So the knowledge of G-d is specifically in the *seder hishtalshelus* (chain of worlds), in *memalei kol almin*. Rabbi Markel adds that, looked at more closely, he thinks it is even more in the lower worlds (*Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*) than higher up; and the name *Havaya* is basically the four worlds, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*.
So *daas* is specifically to be connected with, to have *daas* enter, the comprehension of *memalei kol almin*.

phrases.he: (בל"א דער קלעפ כו' כנ"ל באורך) שהוא דוקא המביא לבחינת עומקא דכולא, דהיינו לעומק דחכמה שמאין תמצא כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: It is specifically this that brings one to the aspect of the “depth of everything,” that is, the depth of *Chochmah* “which is found from nothing,” as explained above.

blocks.text: The Yiddish in the text, “*der klepp*,” he understands as holding on, in the length of the matter.

**It is specifically this that brings one to the aspect of the “depth of everything,”** that is, *hisbonenus* is what brings to it; and what is that? **the depth of *Chochmah* “which is found from nothing,”** the *taalumos chachma* (hidden depths of wisdom) explained before, which come after *hisbonenus*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בבחינת עומק ראיות השכל בהשגה זו דבחינת מלא כל עלמין שלמעלה מהשגת השכל כידוע
phrases.en: In other words, [this is] the depth of the sight of the intellect, into this comprehension of how *HaShem*’s-יהו״ה G-dliness permeates all worlds, which is higher than the [actual] grasp of the intellect, as known.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב ברעיא מהימנא, בעין בשכל, דבלבא אתחזי כולא, ונקרא לאסתכלא ביקרא כו' וגם בזה יש בחינת עומק כנזכר לעיל באריכות)
phrases.en: (This is as stated in *Ra’aya Mehemnah*, “with the eye of the intellect, for the heart sees all.” This is [also] called, “Gazing at the preciousness [of the King].” Now, in this too there is an aspect of depth, as explained above at length.)
notes: See Zohar Miketz 199a, Bereshit 38a-b, Pikudei 247b, Trumah 134a

blocks.text: In other words, **the depth of the sight of the intellect**: seeing the matter with the mind.

This is not the sight of prophecy, which is actually seeing with the eyes. *Re'iyas hasechel*, the sight of the intellect, means that something is explained to a person until he sees its truth: it is no longer an explanation; he actually sees the truth of it.

One might ask: the Rebbe says that even physical sight, pointing with the finger and saying “this,” comes from *hisbonenus*. Everything does come from *hisbonenus*, but what is spoken of here is the sight of the intellect, called the sight of *chachma*.

**This is as stated in *Ra’aya Mehemnah*, “with the eye of the intellect, for the heart sees all.”** With the eye of the intellect within the heart, everything is seen. **This is [also] called, “Gazing at the preciousness [of the King].”** That is, seeing the glory of the King.

**Now, in this too there is an aspect of depth**: as explained before, when one reaches *chachma* there too is a length, a width and a depth, so in the sight of *chachma* too there is a depth. That completes the matter of chapter one.

sections.title: Tevuna: seeing G-dliness in the world
sections.summary: Tevuna draws the hidden depth of memalei kol almin down into what one actually sees, until the physical world itself is seen as G-dliness. It comes from absorbing the concept, going over it until it is part of oneself.

phrases.he: ובחינת התבונה היינו לדלות על ידו מעומק זה הנעלם במושג זה דממלא כל עלמין הנזכר לעיל לידי גילוי, כי בהיותו קולט בכי טוב לעצם ההשגה הזאת, על כן יוכל להביאה בכמה ענינים נבדלים ממנה
phrases.en: Now, the aspect of *Tvunah* is to draw forth from this concealed depth, into revelation in the comprehension of how *HaShem*’s-יהו״ה G-dliness fills all worlds. For, since he grasps the essence of this concept very well, he is, therefore, capable of bringing it into many separate matters.

blocks.text: Now he comes to chapter two.
The whole exile is specifically because of a lack of *tevuna*. It says, “My people does not contemplate”: both are lacking, but more than anything it is a lack of *tevuna*.

Now, **the aspect of *Tvunah* is to draw forth from this concealed depth, into revelation**. Once one reaches the hidden depth, not only the depth of *bina* but the depth of *chachma*, where through the explanation one actually sees, in the mind, how the thing truly is, *tevuna* brings it into revelation.
Here actual seeing with the eye comes in: bringing it down so that one actually sees G-dliness in the physical world, in what is actually happening.
Once a person has the whole understanding, it is no longer abstract; he brings it all the way down into what he is seeing.

There is a story that the Alter Rebbe asked the Mitteler Rebbe what he had *davened* with, and he answered, with a *hisbonenus* about *Adam Kadmon*. Then he asked the Alter Rebbe what he had *davened* with, and the Alter Rebbe answered, with the *shtender*. It was not a joke: he *davened* with seeing that the *shtender* itself is *Elokus*. That is *tevuna*: to look around, apply the whole of the *bina*, and realize that one is looking at nothing but G-d, *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him), and that he was looking at Him all along.

Children's magazines have a picture with ten hidden bunnies to find: among the leaves of a tree, a bunny upside down. Before finding them, one sees the whole picture and every bunny in it, but does not notice them. Once found, or once someone points them out (“here is his nose, here are his feet”), one sees them with his physical eyes, and it is hard to make them look like leaves again. One is not seeing more than before; it is the same picture. So G-d hides, and this book shows us where the bunnies are.

One then says, “Here is the hand of G-d”: *chesed* the right arm, *gevura* the left. When the Jews went out of Egypt, the magicians saw the finger of G-d, and later the hand of G-d was seen. They did not see any hand; they saw a thing that was the hand of G-d.

**For, since he grasps the essence of this concept very well, he is, therefore, capable of bringing it into many separate matters.** It is not enough to understand what the book explains; one must go over it a few more times, until it is absorbed.

phrases.he: כמו בכמה פרטי מציאות עולמות הנבראים, איך שמתהווים מאין ליש בבחינת ממלא דרך פרט אשר נעלם בכללות השגה זו כו'
phrases.en: For example, [he can understand] many details in the existence of the created worlds, how they come into being from nothing to something. [He understands this and draws this out] in a manner of particulars from the general concept of *Memaleh Kol Almin*, in which these particulars were concealed.

blocks.text: **For example, [he can understand] many details in the existence of the created worlds, how they come into being from nothing to something**, details that were **concealed** in the general comprehension he had before, like the bunnies in the picture.

sections.title: Without tevuna: “What is this good for?”
sections.summary: Without tevuna, a person can understand Chassidus well and still not know what to do with it; G-dliness and the world stay two separate things for him. True tevuna sees that there is nothing besides G-d, and that what one really wants is the G-dliness itself.

phrases.he: ובלתי כח התבונה הזאת בהשגה זו שממלא כל עלמין הרי נשארת השגה זו רק במוח הבנתו לבד, ולא ידע מה לעשות בה ואיך להביא זאת ההתבוננות באיכות ענין התהוות היש מאין כלל, כמובן מכל הנזכר לעיל ודי למבין
phrases.en: Without this power of *Tvunah* in this comprehension of *Memaleh Kol Almin*, his comprehension of it would remain in his brain of understanding alone. He would not know what to do with this [concept], or how to bring this *Hitbonenut* to comprehend how [his very own] existence is brought about something from nothing. [He would not be capable of doing this] at all, as understood from all the above. This will suffice for those of understanding.

blocks.text: **Without this power of *Tvunah* in this comprehension of *Memaleh Kol Almin*, his comprehension of it would remain in his brain of understanding alone.** There are many people studying Chassidus who have no *tevuna* in it.
**He would not know what to do with this** concept.

People ask: you learn this kind of Chassidus, but what is it good for? Will it make me money? Will it improve my *middos*? A *mussar* book improves the *middos*, but this is only an intellectual thing, good for people who like puzzles. How does it help the *davenen*?
Nor will he know how to bring this *hisbonenus* into an actual understanding of how the world comes into being, something from nothing, rather than a set of abstract explanations.

phrases.he: (ומזה מובן סיבת המניעה בחדשים או גם בישנים בחסרי תבונה, גם שמשיגים היטב הדק בשעה ששומעים ורואים, לא יוכלו להביא הדבר כלל בהתבוננות בתפלה בענין התהוות העולמות
phrases.en: (From the above we may [now] understand the reason for the lacking [which may be found] in beginners or even in those who are experienced, but lack *Tvunah*. Although they grasp [the explanations of the concepts well], when they hear or read them, they are incapable of bringing the matter of the coming into being of the worlds out of nothing, into contemplation during their prayers.

blocks.text: **From the above we may [now] understand the reason for the lacking [which may be found] in beginners or even in those who are experienced, but lack *Tvunah*.**
They learned Chassidus and understood it; perhaps not every detail, but they understood.

Yet **they are incapable of bringing the matter of the coming into being of the worlds out of nothing, into contemplation during their prayers**: not necessarily in prayer, but in *hisbonenus* as it relates to the actual world.
Because they lack *tevuna*, they also think that *hisbonenus* in *tefilla* means thinking about abstract things during the prayers, sitting and spacing out.

But the height of the whole *tefilla* is asking the *Aibershter*: make me healthy, give me a livelihood, bring us back to Jerusalem, build the Temple. *Baruch* means to draw down: bring Yourself down to here. Revive the dead; forgive us; restore the service in the Temple, and then we can all sit and learn Chassidus the whole time.
*Tefilla* means bringing G-dliness down into the world, asking that it come in actual physical things, asking the *Aibershter* to take over the world and bring Moshiach.
They do not see what contemplating how *Atik* and *Arich* are two sides of the same thing has to do with getting money.

This concerns *avodas halev* and *tefilla*, *avodas hamochin* too, and certainly *daas Havaya*, which will be the real matter of Moshiach: not only during prayer, but in everything one does, to see that nothing happens by accident and that it is literally the *Aibershter* doing it all. One is supposed to see it, not just believe it, as with belief in *hashgacha pratis* (Divine providence).

phrases.he: עד שישאל מה לעשות בכל זה ולאיזה תועלת צריכים לזה כי ב' דברים נבדלים הם לדעתו, מפני שנשאר רק בחינת ההבנה עצמה במוחו, נבדל לגמרי מכל ענין כו' (בל"א מער ניט „ז דער מושכל15 „ליין פ„ר זיך כו') וד"ל16:
phrases.en: [Because of this] they may reach the point where they ask [themselves], “What am I to do with all this?” and “Of what benefit is this [to me].” This is because in his mind these are two separate things, because the understanding remains in his mind [as an abstract concept], totally removed from all matters. This will suffice those of understanding.)

blocks.text: Because of this, **they may reach the point where they ask [themselves], “What am I to do with all this?” and “Of what benefit is this [to me].”** What is all this Chassidus good for?

There is an even higher point: Chassidus is not for the sake of money; when one asks for a livelihood, the Chassidus is the livelihood. What he wants most is the Chassidus itself, and if anything the money is for the Chassidus.

**This is because in his mind these are two separate things**: Chassidus and the world have nothing to do with each other. The world is the world, and on Shabbos one sits with friends and does a crossword puzzle of Chassidus a little.

It is **because the understanding remains in his mind [as an abstract concept], totally removed from all matters**: he has nothing but the idea itself, and it is connected to nothing in the world or in his life.

There are levels here. At one level it is wholly abstract and has nothing to do even with what one asks for in *tefilla*. At another it is used to bring down the light so that one will get things in the world, but it is still two things: there is G-d, and there is the world, and one asks G-d for help. That is already some *tevuna*, that something will come out of it, but it is not the real *tevuna*.

The real *tevuna* is *ein od milvado*: what one really wants is the Chassidus, and he wants health not so that the Chassidus will help his health but the opposite, so that his health and money will help his Chassidus. If we were all healthy and had money, we could all sit together and learn Chassidus all the time. It is all one thing.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between the length and the width of *bina* in contemplating *memalei kol almin*?
Why are the analogies of the movement of an animal, the letters of speech and the flame from the coal called the width of one length?
How does the depth reached after length and width differ from a brief summary, if the two look alike?
What is the sight of the intellect, and how does it differ from the sight of prophecy?
What does the story of the Alter Rebbe *davening* “with the *shtender*,” and the picture of the hidden bunnies, show about *tevuna*?
Why do people who understand Chassidus well still ask, “What am I to do with all this?”, and what is the real *tevuna*?

notes.text: the reader's text and Rabbi Markel's differ: his reads שם אדם, the reader's א״ד (the name Ad-noi). He says the reader's version 'makes more sense' (021 0:52–1:23). The draft follows the printed text and translation (Adnus).
after 'the iyun is the vessel to come to the depth' he adds a half-sentence about 'how the pnimi works in the seder hishtalshelus' later on (021 1:53); unclear, left out.
he refers back to 'the thing we said about the Alter Rebbe or the Deitschel and the dead' (021 5:25), presumably a story from an earlier class; it is not explained here and is left out.
he reads the Yiddish 'der klepp' tentatively ('I think klepp is the holding onto…', 021 9:13); the draft reports it as his reading.
